1.h: Added Articles 31A and 31B and the Ninth Schedule to protect certain laws, added clause (4) to Article 15, replaced Article 19(2), and replaced Articles 85 and 174 on sessions of Parliament and State Legislatures.

3.h: Replaced entry 33 of the Concurrent List in the Seventh Schedule, adding foodstuffs, cattle fodder, raw cotton, cotton seed and raw jute to the trade and production subjects that both Parliament and the States can make laws on.

4.h: Replaced Article 31(2) so that courts could not question a law for taking property on the ground that the compensation was not adequate, and added Article 31(2A). Also replaced Article 31A(1) and Article 305, and added entries 14 to 20 to the Ninth Schedule.

5.h: Replaced the condition in Article 3 on forming new States and changing State boundaries.

6.h: Changed rules on taxing sales of goods: added to Article 269, replaced parts of Article 286, and added Seventh Schedule entries.

7.h: Reorganised the States: replaced the Part A, B, C and D categories with States and Union territories, and replaced Articles 81, 82, 170, 239 and 240. Also added Articles 258A, 290A, 350A and 350B, among others.

9.h: Provided for handing certain border areas to Pakistan under the India-Pakistan agreements of 1958 to 1960, by taking them out of Assam, Punjab, West Bengal and Tripura in the First Schedule from dates to be notified. Only the Punjab part took effect, on 17 January 1961.

10.h: Added Dadra and Nagar Haveli as a Union territory in the First Schedule and under Article 240.

11.h: Had the Vice-President elected by an electoral college of the members of both Houses of Parliament, instead of at a joint meeting of the two Houses (Article 66). Added Article 71(4): a vacancy in the electoral college is no ground to challenge the election of a President or Vice-President.

13.h: Added Article 371A with special provisions for Nagaland and renamed Part XXI to cover special provisions.

14.h: Made Pondicherry a Union territory (First Schedule and Article 240), with effect from 16 August 1962. Added Article 239A so Parliament could create a legislature and Council of Ministers for certain Union territories, raised Lok Sabha seats for Union territories from 20 to 25 (Article 81), and gave Pondicherry a Rajya Sabha seat.

15.h: Raised the retirement age of High Court judges from 60 to 62 (Articles 217 and 224), added Article 224A on retired judges sitting again, and let a High Court issue writs wherever the cause of action arises (Article 226). Also changed Articles 124, 128, 222, 297, 311 and 316.

16.h: Allowed reasonable limits on free speech, assembly and association in the interests of the sovereignty and integrity of India (Article 19). Added a promise to uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India to the oaths in the Third Schedule, and made candidates for Parliament and State Legislatures take an oath (Articles 84 and 173).

17.h: Widened the meaning of “estate” in Article 31A to cover raiyatwari and other farm land, and said land within the ceiling limit that its owner farms personally can be taken only at market value or more. Added entries 21 to 64 to the Ninth Schedule.

18.h: Added to Article 3 on forming new States and changing State boundaries.

19.h: Removed election tribunals from the Election Commission's powers in Article 324.

20.h: Added Article 233A, validating the appointments and judgments of certain district judges.

21.h: Added Sindhi to the list of languages in the Eighth Schedule.

22.h: Added Article 244A allowing an autonomous State for tribal areas in Assam, Article 371B for Assam, and a change to Article 275.

23.h: Extended the time limit for reserved seats and Anglo-Indian nomination in Article 334 from twenty to thirty years. Limited Anglo-Indian nomination to one member per State Assembly (Article 333), and reserved no seats for Scheduled Tribes in Nagaland (Articles 330 and 332).

24.h: Said Parliament may amend any provision of the Constitution under Article 368, and that Article 13 does not apply to such amendments (Articles 13(4), 368(1) and 368(3)). Made it compulsory for the President to give assent to a Bill amending the Constitution.

25.h: Replaced “compensation” with an “amount” in Article 31(2), which courts could not question as too low, and said Article 19(1)(f) does not apply to such laws. Added Article 31C, protecting laws that give effect to the Directive Principles in Article 39(b) and (c).

26.h: Removed privy purses and Rulers' privileges (Articles 291 and 362) and added Article 363A ending recognition of Rulers of Indian States.

27.h: Added Article 371C for the Hill Areas of Manipur and Article 239B, letting Union territory administrators make Ordinances (in force from 30 December 1971). Added Mizoram to Article 239A, and Mizoram and Arunachal Pradesh to Article 240.

28.h: Added Article 312A on changing service conditions of certain officers, and removed Article 314.

29.h: Added entries 65 and 66 to the Ninth Schedule.

30.h: Replaced Article 133(1) on civil appeals from High Courts to the Supreme Court.

31.h: Raised the most Lok Sabha seats for States from 500 to 525 and cut those for Union territories from 25 to 20 (Article 81). Changed the seats reserved for Scheduled Tribes in the North-East (Articles 330 and 332).

32.h: Added Articles 371D and 371E for Andhra Pradesh, removed it from Article 371, and changed a Seventh Schedule entry.

33.h: Said a resignation by an MP or MLA takes effect only when the Speaker or Chairman accepts it, and must be refused if it is not voluntary or genuine (Articles 101 and 190).

34.h: Added entries 67 to 86 to the Ninth Schedule.

35.h: Added Article 2A and a Tenth Schedule (since removed) making Sikkim an associate State of the Union, and changed Articles 80 and 81 to match.

36.h: Made Sikkim a State: added it to the First Schedule, gave it a seat in the Council of States in the Fourth Schedule, and added Article 371F with special provisions for it. Removed Article 2A and the old Tenth Schedule, which had made Sikkim an associate State, and related wording in Articles 80 and 81.

38.h: Added clauses on Ordinances and Emergencies to Articles 123, 213, 239B, 352, 356, 359 and 360; most were removed in 1979.

39.h: Added Article 329A on elections of the Prime Minister and Speaker, replaced Article 71, and added Ninth Schedule entries 87 to 124.

40.h: Replaced Article 297 so that resources in India's territorial waters, continental shelf and exclusive economic zone belong to the Union, with their limits set by Parliament. Also added Ninth Schedule entries 125 to 188.

41.h: Raised the retirement age of members of State and Joint Public Service Commissions in Article 316(2) from sixty to sixty-two years.

42.h: Added "socialist", "secular" and "integrity" to the Preamble, Fundamental Duties (Part IVA), tribunals (Part XIVA) and Articles 39A, 43A and 48A, extended House terms to six years and changed Emergency rules. Its changes to Articles 31C and 368 were struck down.

43.h: Removed Articles 31D, 32A, 131A, 144A, 226A and 228A, and related wording in Articles 145, 226, 228 and 366.

44.h: Removed the right to property from the Fundamental Rights (Articles 19(1)(f) and 31) and added Article 300A, replaced "internal disturbance" with "armed rebellion" in Article 352, kept Articles 20 and 21 in force during an Emergency, and brought House terms back to five years.

45.h: Extended the time limit for reserved seats and special representation in Article 334 from thirty to forty years.

46.h: Added clause (29A) to Article 366 so that works contracts, hire-purchase, hiring out goods and serving food count as sales and can be taxed as sales. Also added a tax on inter-State consignments of goods (Article 269 and Union List entry 92B) and replaced Article 286(3).

47.h: Added entries 189 to 202 to the Ninth Schedule.

49.h: Brought the tribal areas of Tripura under the Sixth Schedule by changing Article 244 and the Fifth and Sixth Schedules, and added paragraph 12AA on how Central and State laws apply there.

50.h: Replaced Article 33 so that Parliament's power to limit Fundamental Rights for the armed forces and police forces also covers staff of intelligence agencies and of their telecommunication systems.

51.h: Narrowed the exceptions in Articles 330 and 332 to the autonomous districts of Assam, so that seats are reserved for Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha elsewhere in the North East and in the Assemblies of Nagaland and Meghalaya.

52.h: Added the Tenth Schedule on disqualification for defection, and linked it to Articles 101, 102, 190 and 191.

53.h: Added Article 371G with special provisions for Mizoram.

54.h: Let Parliament set the salaries of Supreme Court and High Court judges by law (Articles 125 and 221), and raised the salaries in the Second Schedule, for example the Chief Justice of India's from 5,000 to 10,000 rupees a month.

55.h: Added Article 371H with special provisions for Arunachal Pradesh.

56.h: Added Article 371-I with special provisions for Goa.

57.h: Added Article 332(3A), which fixes how many Assembly seats are reserved for Scheduled Tribes in Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Mizoram and Nagaland until seats are readjusted after the first census after 2000.

58.h: Added to Part XXII a provision for an authoritative text of the Constitution in Hindi.

59.h: Added Article 359A, which let an Emergency be declared in Punjab over internal disturbance and let Article 21 be suspended there, and freed the 1987 President's Rule in Punjab from the limits in Article 356(5). The 63rd Amendment removed both in 1990.

60.h: Raised the yearly limit on State taxes on professions, trades and jobs in Article 276(2) from 250 to 2,500 rupees, and removed the exception attached to it.

61.h: Lowered the minimum voting age in Article 326 from twenty-one to eighteen years.

62.h: Extended the time limit for reserved seats and special representation in Article 334 from forty to fifty years.

63.h: Removed Article 359A on Punjab and the condition added to Article 356 on President's Rule.

64.h: Let President's Rule in Punjab, proclaimed on 11 May 1987, last up to three years and six months instead of three years, and freed it from the limits in Article 356(5).

65.h: Set up a National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, replacing Article 338(1) and (2) with new clauses (1) to (9) on its members, duties and powers, and renumbering clause (3) as clause (10).

66.h: Added entries 203 to 257 to the Ninth Schedule.

67.h: Let President's Rule in Punjab, proclaimed on 11 May 1987, last up to four years instead of three years and six months (Article 356(4)).

68.h: Let President's Rule in Punjab, proclaimed on 11 May 1987, last up to five years instead of four (Article 356(4)).

69.h: Added Articles 239AA and 239AB with special provisions for Delhi.

70.h: Let the elected members of the Delhi and Pondicherry Assemblies vote in the election of the President, by adding an Explanation to Article 54. Also added Article 239AA(7)(b), so a law made under Article 239AA(7)(a) does not count as an amendment of the Constitution.

71.h: Added to the list of languages in the Eighth Schedule.

73.h: Added Part IX, The Panchayats, and the Eleventh Schedule on their powers, and added to Article 280 on the Finance Commission.

74.h: Added Part IXA, The Municipalities, and the Twelfth Schedule on their powers, and added to Article 280 on the Finance Commission.

75.h: Added to Article 323B on tribunals for other matters, and relettered its sub-clauses.

76.h: Added entry 257A to the Ninth Schedule.

77.h: Added Article 16(4A), which lets the State reserve posts in promotions for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes who are not adequately represented in its services.

78.h: Added entries 258 to 284 to the Ninth Schedule.

79.h: Extended the time limit for reserved seats and special representation in Article 334 from fifty to sixty years.

80.h: Changed how Union taxes are shared with States: replaced Article 270 and parts of Article 269, and removed Article 272.

81.h: Added Article 16(4B), which lets reserved vacancies left unfilled in a year be carried forward to later years. These carried-forward vacancies do not count toward the fifty per cent limit on reservation for the later year.

82.h: Added a proviso to Article 335 that lets the State relax qualifying marks or lower standards of evaluation for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, for reservation in promotions in Union and State services.

83.h: Added to Article 243M, which lists areas where the Panchayats Part does not apply.

84.h: Replaced the year "2000" and related wording on seat readjustment in Articles 55, 81, 82, 170, 330 and 332.

85.h: Replaced certain words in Article 16 on public employment, with retrospective effect.

86.h: Added Article 21A, the right to free and compulsory education for children aged six to fourteen, replaced Article 45, and added a Fundamental Duty in Article 51A.

87.h: Replaced "1991" as the census year for seat readjustment in Articles 81, 82, 170 and 330.

88.h: Added Article 268A on service tax and a Seventh Schedule entry (92C), but these were never brought into force.

89.h: Added Article 338A, a National Commission for Scheduled Tribes, and limited Article 338 to Scheduled Castes.

90.h: Added to Article 332 on reserved Assembly seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

91.h: Added limits on Ministers to Articles 75 and 164, added Article 361B on paid political posts, and removed Tenth Schedule paragraph 3.

92.h: Added languages to the Eighth Schedule and renumbered its entries to fit them in.

93.h: Added Article 15(5), which lets the State make special provisions for backward classes, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in admission to educational institutions, including private ones, aided or unaided. Minority institutions are left out.

94.h: Changed the States named in Article 164 on Ministers, replacing "Bihar".

95.h: Extended the time limit for reserved seats and special representation in Article 334 from sixty to seventy years.

96.h: Replaced "Oriya" in the Eighth Schedule list of languages.

97.h: Added Part IXB, The Co-operative Societies, and Article 43B on promoting them, and added to Article 19.

98.h: Added Article 371J with special provisions for Karnataka.

99.h: Added Article 124A, a National Judicial Appointments Commission, and changed how judges are appointed; the Supreme Court struck all of it down.

100.h: Changed the First Schedule to carry out the 1974 land boundary agreement with Bangladesh and its 2011 protocol, under which the two countries exchanged enclaves. The changes are to the territories of Assam, West Bengal, Meghalaya and Tripura.

101.h: Added the Goods and Services Tax: new Articles 246A, 269A and 279A (GST Council), with changes to tax Articles and the Seventh Schedule.

102.h: Added Article 338B, a National Commission for Backward Classes, and Article 342A on socially and educationally backward classes.

103.h: Added Article 15(6) and Article 16(6) for economically weaker sections of citizens who are not in the groups that already have reservation. The State may reserve up to ten per cent of seats in educational institutions and of posts in public employment for them, on top of existing reservations.

104.h: Extended reserved seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in Article 334 from seventy to eighty years, and replaced its heading. It kept the seventy-year limit for nominated Anglo-Indian members, so their nomination ended in January 2020.

105.h: Changed Articles 338B, 342A and 366(26C) so that the President's list of socially and educationally backward classes is a Central List, used by the Central Government. Each State and Union territory may make its own list by law, which can differ from the Central List.

106.h: Added Articles 330A, 332A and 334A, reserving about one-third of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies, and added the same for the Delhi Assembly to Article 239AA. The reservation starts only after the first census taken after the Act came into force and a fresh delimitation based on it, and lasts fifteen years unless Parliament extends it.
